name: Superior Semicircular Canal Dehiscence Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Minor and Major Criteria for SSCD Diagnosis

criteria.description: High-resolution CT scan demonstrating dehiscence of the bone overlying the superior semicircular canal
Abnormal vestibular-evoked myogenic potentials (VEMP) with lowered thresholds
Presence of characteristic vestibular and auditory symptoms such as sound- or pressure-induced vertigo
Audiometric evidence of conductive hearing loss with intact tympanic membrane
Exclusion of other causes of vertigo and hearing loss

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: CT confirmation of dehiscence, abnormal VEMP testing, and characteristic clinical symptoms
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires correlation of clinical, audiological, and radiological findings.

pathognomonic.notes: Vertigo induced by pressure changes such as Valsalva maneuver

pathognomonic.symptomName: Autophony (hearing one's own voice or body sounds loudly)

common.notes: Typically mild to moderate with normal tympanic membrane
Sensation of visual blurring during head motion
Sensation of pressure or fullness in the ear

occasional.notes: Hearing heartbeat-like sounds in the ear
Non-specific headache associated with vestibular symptoms

rare.notes: Less common than conductive hearing loss
Rarely reported due to proximity of vestibular structures

rare.symptomName: Vertigo triggered by changes in middle ear pressure

laboratory: Vestibular-evoked myogenic potentials (VEMP) with lowered thresholds and increased amplitudes
imaging: High-resolution computed tomography (CT) of temporal bone showing bony dehiscence over superior semicircular canal
genetic: No established genetic markers; mostly sporadic cases
other: Audiometry showing conductive hearing loss with normal tympanic membrane
Clinical examination revealing Tullio phenomenon and Hennebert sign

distinguishingFeatures: Episodic vertigo lasting 20 minutes to several hours
No bony dehiscence on CT imaging
No superior canal dehiscence on imaging

redFlags: Sudden onset of severe vertigo with hearing loss
Neurological deficits such as facial weakness or numbness
references: Minor LB, Solomon D, Zinreich JS, Zee DS. Sound- and pressure-induced vertigo due to bone dehiscence of the superior semicircular canal. N Engl J Med. 1998;339(12): 746-753.
Ward BK, Carey JP, Minor LB. Superior semicircular canal dehiscence syndrome: lessons from the first 20 years. Front Neurol. 2017;8:177.
Brantberg K, Bergenius J, Tribukait A. Vestibular evoked myogenic potentials in superior semicircular canal dehiscence syndrome. Otol Neurotol. 2003;24(6): 961-967.
